title: Branches and geometric branches at a point are counted by the fibres of the normalization
author: The Stacks Project Authors
source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file varieties.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261011
difficulty_reason: The lemma identifies the number of branches of X at x with the number of inverse images of x in the normalization, and the number of geometric branches with the sum of the separable degrees of the residue field extensions over those inverse images. The proof notes that the assumption that every quasi-compact open has finitely many irreducible components is exactly what makes the normalization defined, identifies the stalk of the pushforward of the structure sheaf as the integral closure of the local ring in the total ring of fractions of its reduction, and observes that because the normalization is integral, the points lying over x correspond to the maximal ideals of that integral closure (proof lines 8588-8601). The result is then read off from the algebraic counterpart of the branch count (proof lines 8602-8604). H2: the translation between the fibre of the normalization and the maximal ideals of the integral closure is the substance.
